newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Coca-Cola to build Uzbek bottling plant.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola to build Uzbek bottling plant.

text.p: The Coca-Cola Company said on Friday it will invest $100 million in the former Soviet republic of Uzbekistan. It said $55 million will be spent on the construction of a bottling plant in the capital Tashkent.

"Coca Cola will be investing $100 million over the next 18 months in Uzbekistan to further develop our local production and distribution," John Sheppard, president of Coca-Cola East Central Europe, told a news conference in Tashkent.
Construction of the bottling plant will begin next month, Sheppard said.
On Friday, Coca-Cola opened a $10 million bottling plant in the Uzbek town of Namangan, its third facility in the largely desert nation of 23 million.
The Tashkent plant, named Coca-Cola Bottlers Tashkent Ltd, will be owned by a joint venture comprising Coca-Cola Export Corp, Uzbekistan's Roz Group and state-owned Uzpisheprom.
Sheppard said the investment was part of a two-year investment plan for the former Soviet republics of the Caucasus and Central Asia totalling $200 million.
